agentRun.finalAnswer:
**Six.** Foundry takes six client retainers per year on purpose, and it's a hard cap, not a target.

Here's why:

- **Founder time is the product.** Past six concurrent retainers, the time-per-client drops below the threshold that makes Foundry's work distinguishable from a standard growth shop. Six is where depth lives.
- **The boredom test.** Foundry refuses work that bores the team, even at scale. Fewer clients means the studio can say no to the wrong work and yes to the kind of repositioning bets the studio exists for.
- **The seventh is a no they owe the team.** Owen tracks the count, the partners say the no. It's a structural commitment, not a preference.
- **Brand work requires real attention.** Every brief requires sitting on three customer calls before a single line is written. That rhythm only holds at the right volume.

The belief has been challenged at least twice (Helmsmark, Week 10; Saltline, Week 9) but has held. The cap is also what keeps pricing selective: six clients a year forces Foundry to pick on fit, not fill the pipeline.
